title: Averages: where they go, and how they're shaped
sub: Real simulations: dice for the law of large numbers, exponential draws for the CLT.

frames.caption: Five people each roll a fair die and track their running average. After 10 rolls the averages are all over the place.
50 rolls: closing in on 3.5, the expected value.
2,000 rolls: every run is within 0.06 of 3.5. The law of large numbers: sample averages converge to the expected value. The typical gap shrinks like 1/√n, so 100× more rolls buy 10× more precision.
Single draws from an exponential distribution: hugely skewed, nothing like a bell curve. (Mean 1, standard deviation 1.)
Average of 2 draws: already less lopsided.
Average of 5: the hump moves toward the middle and the right tail shrinks.
Average of 30: almost exactly the normal curve the central limit theorem predicts (dashed: mean 1, sd 1/√30). Whatever the starting shape (with finite variance), averages end up normal.
